shortDescription: By Emily Ou YongJapanese rubber futures fell for a sixth straight session on Friday, pressured by a stronger yen, and were set for their steepest weekly decline since the week ended June 26.($1 = 155.9900 yen)($1 = 6.7165 Chinese yuan)

children: Japanese rubber futures fell for a sixth straight session on Friday, pressured by a stronger yen, and were set for their steepest weekly decline since the week ended June 26.
The Osaka Exchange (OSE) rubber contract for February delivery
was down 1.2 yen, or 0.28%, at 427.5 yen ($2.74) per kg, as of 0144 GMT.
The contract has fallen 3.41% so far this week.
The rubber contract on the Shanghai Futures Exchange (SHFE) for January delivery
rose 125 yuan, or 0.67%, to 18,845 yuan ($2,805.78) per metric ton.
The most-active October butadiene rubber contract on the SHFE (SHBRv1) gained 65 yuan, or 0.44%, to 14,995 yuan per ton.

clung to its gains against the U.S. dollar on Friday and was on track for its strongest week in more than a month, as traders ramped up bets on a Bank of Japan interest rate hike and broader currency markets awaited U.S. payrolls data.
A stronger Japanese currency makes yen-denominated assets less affordable to overseas buyers.
The El Niño weather phenomenon is set to strengthen further into 2027, raising risks of extreme weather into next year, the World Meteorological Organization said on Thursday.
The development poses a longer-term supply risk for rubber-producing regions, analysts from Chinese broker Everbright Futures said in a note.
The front-month rubber contract on Singapore Exchange's SICOM platform for November delivery (STFX6) last traded at 233.4 U.S. cents per kg, up 0.8%.
